_note: L -> W calibration for THIS stack: it is the identity, on purpose.
Why it is not the bridge's default: `bridge_node.load_calib()` falls back to
+90 deg yaw (L's x axis is taken to be the body's forward axis, pointing North,
while W is ENU). That is right for the lio_avoid construction, where the LIO
initialises its world body-aligned. It is WRONG here: our relay publishes ONE
world-aligned ENU frame on /lio/robo/odom, /lio/odom and /lidar_slam/odom, and
SUPER plans in that same frame, so L == W numerically and the only remaining
step is the W(ENU) -> NED permutation the transport applies itself.
Getting this wrong does not look like a crash: a +90 deg yaw maps the 15 m
square onto itself, so the vehicle still visits four corners -- just mirrored,
through different trunks. The score would pass or fail on luck.
The real-aircraft counterpart of this file is the parked-window measurement in
the supervisor (T6 in FRAMES.md); here the frame identity is a design fact, not
a measurement, so it is recorded as such.
